newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais bet millions on polls outcome in Bangkok.
newsitem.headline: Thais bet millions on polls outcome in Bangkok.

text.p: Thai punters have placed millions of dollars in bets on the outcome of Sunday's general election, according to local bookies.
They said about 500 million baht ($20 million) had been staked so far on the November 17 race which surveys indicate will be a close one. Betting opened on Monday.

Opinion polls show that the New Aspiration Party (NAP) of outgoing Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and the Democrat Party of former premier Chuan Leekpai are neck and neck in the race to win most of the 393 lower House of Representative seats up for grabs in the election.
A new survey published by The Nation newspaper on Wednesday forecast that the Democrats were set to win 132 seats in the polls with the NAP coming second with 122 seats.
A total of 2,310 candidates from 13 political parties are vying for the parliamentary seats.
"The odds are 10 to nine for both the Democrats and the NAP to win the general election," a bookie said, adding that the odds were very narrow because of the tight race.

As the Democrats appear on the verge of winning most of the 37 seats being fought over in Bangkok, the bookies said they had set odds of 10 to nine on the Democrat Party winning at least 25 seats out of the 37 at stake.
If the Democrats win at least 25 seats, punters will rake in the money, the bookies said.
Orathai Kanchanachoosak, a candidate for the Palang Dharma Party, in Bangkok told a panel discussion earlier this week that betting has been heavy in her constituency.
